objective: Test whether JANUS can treat representation packages as exact semantic objects with theorem/receipt-backed operation capabilities, conserved deferred debt, and lifecycle-aware route planning without promoting UNKNOWN to cheap or hiding unsupported operations behind compact syntax.
package_type: K_PACKAGE = (L, theta, K, semantics_ref, Gamma_L, paid_costs, debt_ledger, provenance)

R3B_A.name: CAPABILITY_MAP_FREEZE
R3B_A.pass: Every listed operation has an explicit capability_status and proof_status; UNKNOWN remains first-class; external theorem evidence is not internal receipt authority.

R3B_B.name: CLOSURE_HARDNESS_KILLER
R3B_B.pass: For STRUCTURED_D_DNNF + EXISTS_SINGLE, planner must not promise same-language polynomial closure and must return either an exact certified escape route or NO_CERTIFIED_CHEAP_ROUTE.

R3B_C.name: CAPABILITY_AWARE_ESCAPE
R3B_C.pass: For trajectories where exact relaxation to DNNF preserves required future operations, planner may use it only after charging translation and preserving provenance; routes that lose a required future capability must be rejected.

R3B_D.name: DEFERRED_DEBT_ATTACK
R3B_D.pass: DEFERRED_WITH_DEBT must increase D; UNKNOWN upper bound blocks polynomial lifecycle claim; debt may decrease only with a discharge receipt.

R3B_E.name: MULTI_OPERATION_PLANNER
R3B_E.pass: Planner must choose routes by total certified lifecycle status/cost across the frozen trajectory, not by current node count or one-step operation cost. It must allow NO_CERTIFIED_CHEAP_ROUTE as a correct outcome.

debt_law: D_next = D_current + D_incurred - D_discharged; every discharge requires replayable receipt.
